objectives.description: Container measures, proportions and limit-based comparison.

objectives.description: Specialized measurement, shapes, material, consistency and surface qualities.
objectives.rationale: Generic weight, capacity, area, shape, hardness, moisture, material, taste and cleanliness inventories have no corresponding A1 general-notion set in checked columns. H owns any immediate food/item context individually; A2-F owns general extensions. Do not infer that every concrete noun is A1.

objectives.description: Posture, nested position and detailed route-change contrasts.
objectives.rationale: The enumerated A1 location/motion set precedes standing/sitting, above/below/inside/outside and route-change verbs in the A2 column. Planned traer is explicitly proposed A2; its prior A1 record is not discarded.

objectives.description: Elapsed, simultaneous and phase-related time beyond routine sequence.
objectives.rationale: A1 includes clock/calendar anchors, simple before/after, start/end/repeat and basic recurrence. Since/until/during, ago, already/still, simultaneous relations and have-just/still-doing constructions belong A2 selection; not missing A1 synonyms to pad counts.

objectives.description: Abstract adequacy, utility, importance and generalized normality.
objectives.rationale: Checked A1 entries support concrete good/bad, value, attractiveness, interest and difficulty. A2 owns abstract useful/useless, important, suitable and normal/different judgments. A1 saber skill and poder practical ability remain explicit context-level proposals.

objectives.description: Productive later pronoun, determiner and clause systems.
objectives.rationale: Independent possessives, generalized direct/indirect clitics and combinations, emphatic object pronouns, distributive each/every, full indefinite systems, comparisons, conditional clauses and productive temporal subordination are not A1 lexical scope. Forms of selected meanings are not new senses; ordinal apocope is noted as later productive grammar.

objectives.description: Form-level obligations rather than additional lexical senses.
objectives.rationale: Unresolved shared authoring prerequisite: validate noun/adjective/article agreement, negative/interrogative frame, selected present-indicative forms and question/statement intonation across F/P/H/T/W/C/S/D. comer and vivir link regular -er/-ir models; hablar links -ar. Grammar tables or every inflected token must not inflate sense counts.

objectives.description: Body, age, perception aids and personal attributes used by general notions.
objectives.rationale: A1-P owns explicit person/body selections including baseline es-sk:a1:025-delgado, es-sk:a1:058-edad, es-sk:a1:075-hombre, es-sk:a1:076-mujer, es-sk:a1:077-nino and new gafas/gordo decisions. Cross-cell closure is unresolved until P adjudication; F does not replace their meaning-level review. alto/bajo, gustar/querer/conocer/vivir are linked where relevant.

objectives.description: Purchase, value, object access and concrete item attributes.
objectives.rationale: A1-H owns food-taking tomar (a1-actions-planned-05), color/price labels, open/close access and concrete home/shop contrasts. F links relevant baseline senses; entrada ticket es-sk:a1:304-entrada is not automatically a physical entrance, so H/T must adjudicate a new entrance sense. This dependency remains open until those cells close.

objectives.description: Map orientation, entry/exit signs and geographic direction.
objectives.rationale: A1-T owns routes, left/right/straight, entrance/exit and transport contexts; A1-S owns north/south/east/west geographic labels and four seasons. F crosslinks five existing direction entries and four seasons, proposes east/west noun senses for S ownership and preserves demonstrative este separately. All linked cell decisions remain unresolved until adjudicated.

objectives.description: Classroom interaction and mental/verbal functions.
objectives.rationale: A1-W owns read/write/understand/repeat and classroom applications; A1-C owns ordinary media/conversation contexts; A1-P owns mental state distinctions such as pensar and recordar, including any proposed A2 introduction. F links baseline verbs without asserting generic A1 approval for every meaning of their lemma.

objectives.description: Social functions and context-bound formula choices.
objectives.rationale: A1-D owns all five a1-social-planned-01 through a1-social-planned-05 formulas (perdón, lo siento, de nada, buenos días, hasta luego), permission/help, repair, acknowledgment and de acuerdo/vale decisions. F handles composition and propositional sí/no/bien/mal, not every pragmatic function of the same word. D closure is unresolved.

selections.sense: identify a person or attribute a basic characteristic
selections.levelRationale: Identity and simple classification are required before any personal-information exchange.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: Introduce the copular sense, not advanced passive or emphatic uses.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic unless a form note states regional variation; es-ES audio
selections.formNotes: Irregular soy, eres, es, somos, sois, son; attribute agreement; profession usually without article.
selections.pronunciationNotes: One syllable; preserve final r in isolated infinitive.

selections.sense: state where or when an event takes place
selections.levelRationale: A learner must locate a class or appointment without confusing event ser with object estar.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: New event-location use of the existing identity lemma, not a harder example of identity.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic unless a form note states regional variation; es-ES audio
selections.formNotes: Same ser paradigm; event subject plus time/location complement.
selections.pronunciationNotes: Connected es el and es en need phrase-boundary listening.
uncertainties: Global sense-granularity review must distinguish this construction from basic identity.

selections.sense: be located somewhere or be in a current state
selections.levelRationale: Current whereabouts support immediate needs and contrast with stable identification.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: Retain basic location/state introduction; idiomatic and progressive uses are separate.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic unless a form note states regional variation; es-ES audio
selections.formNotes: Irregular estoy, estás, está, estamos, estáis, están; temporary-state versus event-location notes.
selections.pronunciationNotes: Written accents in estás/está/están; no initial extra vowel.

selections.sense: state impersonal existence using hay
selections.levelRationale: Recognizing existence or absence of a needed service is a minimal A1 function.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: Keep existential hay distinct from auxiliary haber in compound tenses.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic unless a form note states regional variation; es-ES audio
selections.formNotes: Hay is impersonal and invariant with plural objects; bare or indefinite noun phrase.
selections.pronunciationNotes: Silent h; hay is one syllable, distinct spelling from ahí.

selections.sense: have or possess a thing
selections.levelRationale: Possession completes simple statements about personal resources.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: Concrete possession precedes obligation and idiomatic tener constructions.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic unless a form note states regional variation; es-ES audio
selections.formNotes: Tengo, tienes, tiene; no English-style have got calque; bare noun possible.
selections.pronunciationNotes: Stress tengo on first syllable, tener on last; g has hard value.

selections.sense: mark a possessor or owner
selections.levelRationale: Naming whose familiar object it is makes elementary identification useful.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: Retain possession, distinguish origin/material and temporal starts.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic unless a form note states regional variation; es-ES audio
selections.formNotes: Unstressed before possessor; de + el contracts to del unless el belongs to a title/proper-name exception.
selections.pronunciationNotes: Reduced prominence in noun phrase; do not stress every function word.

selections.sense: mark a person's geographical origin
selections.levelRationale: Answering where someone comes from is part of first introductions.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: Different relation from the existing possession sense of de.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic unless a form note states regional variation; es-ES audio
selections.formNotes: Ser de plus place; no gender inflection; nationality adjectives belong P/S.
selections.pronunciationNotes: Short unstressed de links to following place without inserted pause.
uncertainties: Shared lemma must retain sense links rather than overwrite possession.

selections.sense: identify a known masculine singular referent
selections.levelRationale: Definite reference allows a learner to identify the object already under discussion.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: Retain article meaning; pronoun él and generic advanced uses are separate.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic unless a form note states regional variation; es-ES audio
selections.formNotes: Forms la, los, las; contractions al/del; no standalone article before profession in basic ser statements.
selections.pronunciationNotes: Unstressed el contrasts with stressed pronoun él despite same segments.

selections.sense: introduce one unspecified member of a noun category
selections.levelRationale: First mention of an unfamiliar object requires an indefinite determiner.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: Article function differs from standalone cardinal uno, despite shared historical form.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic unless a form note states regional variation; es-ES audio
selections.formNotes: Forms una, unos, unas; agreement with noun; do not count forms as separate senses.
selections.pronunciationNotes: Normally unstressed; una has initial-syllable stress when isolated.

selections.sense: identify a nearby referent before its noun
selections.levelRationale: Pointing to an object close to the speaker supports a basic identification task.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: Spatial demonstrative, not directional east or later anaphoric use.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic unless a form note states regional variation; es-ES audio
selections.formNotes: Esta, estos, estas; no preceding article; temporal extension reviewed in A2.
selections.pronunciationNotes: First-syllable stress; no written accent for normal demonstrative use.

selections.sense: identify a referent at the listener's location or a less near distance
selections.levelRationale: The intermediate distance contrast prevents reducing every pointing expression to este.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: Completes basic spatial deixis without adding discourse-anaphoric meaning.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic unless a form note states regional variation; es-ES audio
selections.formNotes: Esa, esos, esas; pre-nominal agreement; distance is contextual not measured meters.
selections.pronunciationNotes: First-syllable stress; maintain both clear e vowels.

selections.sense: identify a referent distant from both speaker and listener
selections.levelRationale: A distinct far-distance determiner supports elementary three-way pointing.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: Contrast with near este and intermediate ese, not anaphoric reference to old discourse.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic unless a form note states regional variation; es-ES audio
selections.formNotes: Aquella, aquellos, aquellas; do not attach an article before demonstrative.
selections.pronunciationNotes: Final stress in aquel, penultimate in aquella; qu is k, ll dialect note.

selections.sense: refer to a nearby unidentified thing without naming its category
selections.levelRationale: Asking what an unknown object is requires reference before its noun/gender is known.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: Neuter reference is not a feminine/masculine form of a noun determiner.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic unless a form note states regional variation; es-ES audio
selections.formNotes: Invariable neuter singular; no following noun; basic qué es esto frame.
selections.pronunciationNotes: First syllable stressed; final o remains clear.

selections.sense: refer to an unidentified thing at a less near distance
selections.levelRationale: The learner can ask about a pointed-out object without assigning grammatical gender.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: Neuter counterpart to ese for an unidentified referent, not textual anaphora.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic unless a form note states regional variation; es-ES audio
selections.formNotes: Invariable; used without noun; no plural form for this sense.
selections.pronunciationNotes: First syllable stressed; avoid Slovak vowel-length substitution.

selections.sense: refer to an unidentified thing far from both participants
selections.levelRationale: Completes the far-distance unknown-object question set.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: Different distance from esto/eso, not a new sense for every object pointed at.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic unless a form note states regional variation; es-ES audio
selections.formNotes: Invariable neuter; no noun after it.
selections.pronunciationNotes: Stress middle syllable; qu hard k and ll voiced palatal variety acknowledged.

selections.sense: mark something belonging to the speaker
selections.levelRationale: Personal possessions and family relations require first-person possessive reference.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: Attributive possessive before a noun; independent mío belongs later.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic unless a form note states regional variation; es-ES audio
selections.formNotes: Mis in plural; no gender variation; not combined with definite article.
selections.pronunciationNotes: Unaccented mi contrasts with stressed mí after prepositions.

selections.sense: mark something belonging to one familiar addressee
selections.levelRationale: Asking about the listener's details requires second-person possession.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: Possessive tu differs from existing subject pronoun tú.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic unless a form note states regional variation; es-ES audio
selections.formNotes: Tus in plural; no gender variation; noun follows.
selections.pronunciationNotes: No written accent; typically unstressed before noun.

selections.sense: mark something belonging to a third person or formal addressee
selections.levelRationale: Formal service exchanges and third-person descriptions need possession beyond mi/tu.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: Ambiguous owner is resolved by context, not by inventing a separate form for each person.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic unless a form note states regional variation; es-ES audio
selections.formNotes: Sus in plural; owner may be él, ella, usted, ellos or ustedes; de + name clarifies.
selections.pronunciationNotes: One unstressed syllable; retain clear u.

selections.sense: mark something belonging to a group including the speaker
selections.levelRationale: Describing a shared home or class requires group possession.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: Group-owner meaning contrasts with mi; possessive agrees with possessed noun.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic unless a form note states regional variation; es-ES audio
selections.formNotes: Nuestra, nuestros, nuestras; preverbal versus pronominal uses not conflated.
selections.pronunciationNotes: Nue is a diphthong; first syllable stressed.

selections.sense: mark something belonging to familiar plural addressees in Spain
selections.levelRationale: An es-ES course needs comprehension of plural familiar ownership.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: Regional counterpart to su with ustedes, not the only pan-Hispanic choice.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic unless a form note states regional variation; es-ES audio
selections.formNotes: Vuestra, vuestros, vuestras; primarily Spain with vosotros.
selections.pronunciationNotes: Vue diphthong; v pronounced like b, not Slovak v.

selections.sense: refer to oneself as the speaker and grammatical subject
selections.levelRationale: A first self-introduction establishes who is speaking.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: Basic participant deixis, not emphasis or topicalization strategies.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic unless a form note states regional variation; es-ES audio
selections.formNotes: Usually optional with inflected verb; no gender/plural paradigm within this person.
selections.pronunciationNotes: Single stressed syllable; initial y has accepted regional realizations.

selections.sense: address one familiar person as grammatical subject
selections.levelRationale: Peer conversation requires recognition of familiar singular address.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: Subject tú contrasts with possessive tu and formal usted.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic unless a form note states regional variation; es-ES audio
selections.formNotes: No gender forms; second-person singular agreement; vos is a regional alternative, not an extra A1 production paradigm here.
selections.pronunciationNotes: Written accent distinguishes possessive; clear u.

selections.sense: address one person with formal or respectful treatment

exclusions.reason: Select first through tenth only; gender, plural and primer/tercer forms are not separate senses. Higher ordinals, generic fractions, percentages and numerical scientific notation belong later inventories.

exclusions.reason: Select nine literal color bases plus light/dark; all seven weekdays/twelve months/four seasons; clock hours 0–23 and minute values 0–59 through selected cardinal composition, with 12-hour spoken quarter/half/exact frames. Regional vos remains a labeled form obligation, not an extra uncontrolled paradigm or fictitious es-ES standard.

exclusions.reason: PCIC is the acknowledged framework; these English editorial sense glosses and judgments are original Wordfold selections. No certification, endorsement or license for bulk reproduction is inferred.

coverageNotes: Selection enumeration for the bounded A1-F scenarios is ready for independent coverage review; status remains proposed. No full-course completion, exact unique freeze, native signoff or learner-content publication is claimed.

Rows are local proposals, not production IDs. All 685 baseline records and all 138 exact next-selection records were inspected for relevant identity matching. Forty-three planned IDs are linked here: 38 A1 non-social selections plus five A2 comparison boundary records. The five remaining A1 social IDs belong D explicitly; other levels/topics are not forced into F.

Cardinals comprise 48 numerical bases plus the separate noun número; 10 ordinal senses; 7 weekdays; 12 months; 4 season crosslinks. Stated composition bounds are authoring/QA requirements, not separately counted learner words. Derived totals depend on accepted sense/form policy.

Same-lemma meanings remain distinct: ser identity/event location; de possession/origin/span start; a destination/time; en location/calendar; mañana morning/tomorrow; tarde afternoon/late; segundo ordinal/time unit; tiempo weather-linked baseline versus new temporal sense; metro transport-linked baseline versus length unit; naranja fruit-linked baseline versus color; qué pronoun/determiner; mucho/poco/bastante quantity/degree; este demonstrative/east. Existing references on select-new rows identify collision history, not permission to overwrite.

Gender/person forms are normally paradigms: ella is accounted for by exact a1-identity-planned-04 on él with an explicit merge uncertainty; ellos/ellas and subject plural address need global sense-policy review. Independent identical spellings with different syntactic or semantic roles are not automatically one sense.

Existing oír is proposed A2; previously planned A1 mirar and traer are proposed A2 without dropping their original IDs. Several other placement tensions between grammar/general-notion columns remain explicit per row; PCIC is not claimed to certify any Wordfold word-level decision.

Cross-reference rows are not net-new counts. Prerequisite objectives name unresolved cross-cell authoring/ownership requirements; they cannot be treated as closed simply because F has a matching lemma. Any omission judged required during independent review becomes deferred-core and blocks full inventory completion.

Pronunciation notes are written risk analysis: syllable/stress, accent, hiatus/diphthong, silent h, tap/trill, ñ, sibilant variants and phrase grouping. Every authored item still needs Spanish and Slovak review; physical es-ES routing/playback and risk-stratified listening remain separate gates. No paid synthesis or remote build was run.
